```python
temp = "hello=good="

# Split only at the first '=' so the rest of the string (including the trailing '=') stays together
parts = temp.split('=', 1)

print(parts)   # → ['hello', 'good=']
```

`str.split(sep, maxsplit)` splits the string at most `maxsplit` times.  
Using `maxsplit=1` ensures only the first `=` is used as the delimiter, giving you the desired list `["hello", "good="]`.
